reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis assumes that Mg-rich intermetallics will partition Ti and Zn to grain boundaries to form a protective TiO2/ZnO film, but Mg-rich phases typically deplete the matrix of Mg and do not necessarily drive Ti/Zn segregation, and TiO2/ZnO formation at 600°C in a Mg-containing alloy is chemically questionable without evidence.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and includes specific characterization and performance metrics, but the falsification criterion (>20% improvement) is arbitrary and does not directly test the claimed mechanism of intermetallic-mediated element partitioning.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis addresses a relevant pathway for microstructural control in lightweight HEAs, but the mechanistic link between Mg-rich precipitates and protective oxide formation is speculative and not well-supported, limiting its immediate utility.
